note: Mamluk sultans Baybars and Qalawun systematically dismantled the remaining Crusader states; Caesarea (1265), Jaffa (1268), Krak des Chevaliers (1271), and Acre (1291) fell in a methodical campaign that ended the Crusader presence in the Holy Land.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Mamluk systematic dismantlement of the Crusader coastal strip (1265–1291) permanently eliminated Western European territorial presence in the Levant and closed the two-century chapter of Latin Christian sovereignty in the Holy Land; the subsequent shift in Crusade ideology toward trade embargoes and naval strategy represented the pragmatic recognition that territorial reconquest was no longer achievable.
